title: I've gone cold on someone and I don't know why
blurb: For when someone you were genuinely into stopped landing, with no event that explains it.
entry_signals: I suddenly don't want to be around them
I think I made a mistake about this person
I feel nothing for them now

steps.ask: How much of your energy right now is going into being annoyed that you can't just get on with things?
steps.help: Not how sad you are — that reading is often unavailable. This one is usually more honest: impatience with yourself, frustration that you can't perform at the level you've decided is required.
cites: Forcing Your Inner State To Conform

steps.title: That reading matters more than it looks
steps.say:
That level of self-impatience is usually the signal that distress is already high — it just isn't arriving labelled as distress.

The version of the top of this scale on your side isn't a spiral, it's burning yourself down until you stop registering the discomfort. Nothing decided from there is a decision about the relationship.

Come back when there's some slack. The question below will keep.
cites: I Can Protect Myself But Not Comfort Myself

steps.ask: Before we look at the pattern: is there something real here — something you'd tell a friend to leave over?
steps.help: This is the mirror of the question the other flow asks, and it exists for the same reason. Deactivation can switch off attraction for no reason. It can also switch on for a very good one, and a tool that always says "that's just your avoidance" would talk you out of accurate judgement.

options.label: I can't tell, and that's the problem
No — nothing happened, that's what's strange

steps.title: Then it's information, not a symptom
steps.say:
If there's an actual reason, this flow would only teach you to distrust a working instrument.

People genuinely do conclude, on evidence, that someone isn't right for them — and that conclusion arriving is not proof of avoidance. The tell isn't that you want to leave, it's that the wanting arrived without a reason attached.

You have a reason. Take it at face value.

steps.help_a: Dates and events. When did it turn, and what was going on around then — in the relationship, and in the rest of your life.
steps.ask_b: And what do you now think about them that you didn't before?
steps.help_b: The judgements, in the words you've actually been using. Including the unflattering ones.

steps.ask: Around the time it turned — had anything shifted in how much you two depend on each other?
steps.help: Deactivation is rarely random. It usually follows the point where your system registered that it had got used to someone.

options.label: Yes — things got closer, or more official
Yes — logistics changed. Moving in, more time, more expected of me
No, nothing changed that I noticed

steps.ask: Look at what you wrote about them. Does any of it read as looking down on them?
steps.help: Not an accusation — a diagnostic. Contempt is often what surfaces when something landed as hurt and the hurt never made it into awareness. If it's there, it's pointing at something.

options.label: Yes, honestly — some of it does
No, it reads more like flatness than judgement

steps.ask: Then: did they do anything recently that would have hurt, if you'd let it?
steps.help: Small counts. A promise not kept, being deprioritised, a thing you'd decided not to mind. The question isn't whether it was reasonable to mind — it's whether you did.

steps.ask: What would you need to know to tell the difference between "this person isn't right" and "my system switched off"?
steps.help: Something checkable. One useful test: were the things you now dislike visible to you before, and did you rate them differently then?

steps.ask: What do you actually get from this relationship?
steps.help: This one is harder than it sounds, and its difficulty is the point. If only the costs are legible, the ledger can only ever read as loss — and leaving will look rational every time.

steps.ask: The thing you want here — can you do it, or would they have to agree to it?
steps.help: Worth separating, because withdrawing quietly and setting a boundary look identical from the outside and are not the same act.

options.label: Something I can do on my own
Something they'd have to agree to
I want to say nothing and let it fade

steps.say: Your words, not a verdict. Nothing here says stay or go — only that a decision made while the appraisal program is offline is worth making twice.
